---
name: TBS5530 Hardware and USB Protocol
description: Use for TBS5530 USB firmware, Cypress FX2 bridge, I2C, CXD2878/CXD6802/Ascot3, M88RS6060, DVB frontend and MPEG-TS capture tasks.
---
# TBS5530-specific hardware rules

- Device VID:PID `734c:5530`. Verify the active attachment and raw descriptors at runtime, distinguishing default FX2 from post-firmware operational state. Historical operational endpoints include Bulk IN `0x82`/`0x81`, max packet 512 bytes at High-Speed. Historic WSL interface claim only proved enumeration, **not** DVB or TS streaming. The latest Android tests reached Sony `0x197`, K36 AUTO PLP lock, but no TS bytes and negative native URB completion statuses; read newest project records rather than older unverified labels.
- Prioritize official `tbsdtv/linux_media` as the primary board protocol reference. **Also compare `CoreELEC/linux-amlogic` as a Linux kernel integration/alternative implementation** with its own exact SHA, `drivers/media/usb/dvb-usb/tbs5530.c`, `drivers/media/dvb-frontends/cxd2878.c`, their headers, and Kconfig/Makefile. Include community `koreapyj/cxd28xx` and Go `Till0196/coax` as cross-checks. Use `.github/instructions/coreelec-driver-research.instructions.md` and `.github/skills/tbs-research/SKILL.md` for differential investigations.
- Compare at minimum: firmware image/hash and A0 reset/re-enumeration; I2C bridge transactions `0x80`, `0x90`, `0x91`; frontend chip identity, reset/init, CXD6802/ASCOT3I, auto PLP and TS output registers; stream selection `0x8A` with documented terrestrial payload `0A 00`; endpoint/interface/alt-setting, CLEAR_HALT, URB setup, queue depth and 4096-byte buffers; kernel cleanup/driver lifetime.
- The **CoreELEC TBS5530 driver source defines eight 4096-byte Bulk URBs on endpoint `0x82`** and `0x8A` terrestrial control; this is SOURCE-CONFIRMED for the inspected revision, not RUNTIME-OBSERVED on a specific CoreELEC box. Matching request sizes do not prove identical host setup, FIFO state or URB completion behavior.
- CoreELEC is a separate Linux distribution/kernel for selected Amlogic devices, not an Android app or a generic stock Android USB driver. Source availability is not proof that every CoreELEC image enables the driver or that any specific box has successfully received MPEG-TS with this tuner.
- USB `-EOVERFLOW` / `-EPROTO` requires host-specific completion and control-sequence evidence. Do not blame RF, PLP, power, cable or Android kernel by inference alone. Compare cold-start Windows BDA, Linux (WSL2 or VM), CoreELEC source and Android sequences; mark unknown fields as unknown, not zero. See `.github/instructions/usb-capture-windows.instructions.md`, `usbipd-wsl.instructions.md` and `tsduck-windows.instructions.md`.
- Read-only enumeration, source review and fake/offline tests are allowed. Firmware/vendor/I2C writes require an authorized scoped session; an unchanged grant may cover verified RAM/bootstrap, terrestrial init, K36 auto tune and receive-only operations together under `autonomous-debug.instructions.md` without per-transfer confirmation. Unreviewed writes, uncertain firmware recovery, power cycles, LNB voltage, changing mode/driver and USB ownership transfers require a separate decision.
- Do not use Windows BDA and Linux/WSL/VM as simultaneous owners. Re-read `usbipd list` for live BUSID, respect known USBPcap filter conflicts, and preserve rollback for any host transfer. USB passthrough or a VM does not by itself install the TBS5530 driver.
- Respect GPL source licensing and verify firmware redistribution permission before bundling firmware in an APK or public Git repository.
